questions.question: Using the trailer hand brake during a trailer jackknife will:
questions.explanation: During a trailer jackknife, release the brakes to help your tires regain grip. Using the trailer hand brake will only make the skid worse.

questions.question: If you are not sure if a trailer has ABS, you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Drive on a slippery surface and see if ABS activates.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers made on or after March 1, 1998 must have ABS. You can tell if older trailers have ABS by looking under them for wheel speed sensor wires connected to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: To reduce the risk of a rollover, you should:

options.text: Load cargo as far forward as possible.
Load cargo as far back as possible.
Load cargo as low as possible.
Stack cargo as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load cargo as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load your cargo as close to the ground as possible to reduce rollover risk. Also, take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: The emergency air line:

options.text: Is controlled by the foot brake.
Is connected to the relay valves.
Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) does two things. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: Starting in which year were new trailers required to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: To test the trailer service brakes, you should:

options.text: Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the brake pedal.
Reverse slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.
Reverse slowly and apply the brakes with the brake pedal.
Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.
questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, first make sure the air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Then move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control. You should feel the trailer brakes activate if they are working properly.

questions.question: While inspecting a coupling, you should go under the trailer and:

options.text: Detach the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the emergency position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: A tractor protection valve is:

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or has a bad leak.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that helps the battery recharge.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or has a bad leak.
questions.explanation: On combination vehicles with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, you should:
questions.explanation: Following the correct steps for coupling and uncoupling trailers is important for safe operation. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: The easiest way to know your trailer is skidding is to:

options.text: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer has left its lane.
Release the brake pedal and push it down again.
Watch the jackknife warning light on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer has left its lane.
questions.explanation: The easiest way to spot a trailer skid is to check your mirrors. When you brake hard, always check your mirrors to make sure your trailer is still in the correct position.

questions.question: If a trailer's spring brakes do not release when you push the tractor air supply control, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, make sure all equipment works properly. If the trailer's spring brakes do not release, check that all air line connections are tight and sealed correctly.

questions.question: What is the best way to notice your trailer is starting to skid?
questions.explanation: The best way to spot a trailer skid early is to watch your mirrors. You will see the trailer move off course in the mirror.

questions.question: Trailers with low ground clearance are hard to drive:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings can be difficult to cross with a low-clearance trailer. Low trailers and long trailers pulled by single-axle tractors have special trouble crossing raised railroad crossings.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line or signal line. It carries air to the trailer brakes and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: What is one way to prevent a rollover?

options.text: Move cargo to the left side of the rig.
Keep cargo centered on the rig.
Move cargo to the right side of the rig.
Keep cargo as far from the ground as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cargo centered on the rig.
questions.explanation: Uneven cargo loading can cause a rollover. Keep the load centered on the rig to help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the driver in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you drive too fast. To reduce rollover risk, load cargo low, and take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: What should a driver do to prevent a rollover?
questions.explanation: Rollovers can happen when you turn too quickly. Keep the vehicle's center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: What happens when a combination vehicle goes around a corner?

options.text: The turn should be made as tightly as possible.
The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
The rear wheels should run over the curb.
It is acceptable for street signs to be knocked over if they are too close to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. Trailers make this effect more noticeable.

questions.question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Removing the parking brake control knob.
Releasing air with the brake pedal.
Releasing air with the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully, turn off the engine, then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when the air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When are rollovers most likely to happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too fast. Slow down before entering turns and curves, especially when your rig is fully loaded.
